newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Shots fired as political rivals clash in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Shots fired as political rivals clash in Zaire.

text.p: Supporters of two Zairean opposition leaders clashed in the capital Kinshasa on Saturday, firing shots and throwing stones, witnesses said.

A spokesman for politician Frederic Kibassa Maliba said two bodyguards of Kibassa, who leads a breakaway faction of the opposition alliance led by former prime minister Etienne Tshisekedi, were wounded in the clash in the city's Limete district.

"Supporters of Mr Tshisekedi arrived this morning at their party headquarters for a meeting. But they wanted to prevent Mr Kibassa's supporters from entering his house which is situated just next door," Prospere Ndume, Kibassa's spokesman told Reuters.
Witness Mubenga Amand said Kibassa's bodyguards responded by opening fire into the air.
Tshisekedi's supporters have given a warning of trouble in Kinshasa if the radical opposition leader is not brought back to the position of prime minister.
A new crisis government was expected to be announced by President Mobutu Sese Seko later on Saturday to deal with a Tutsi-led rebellion in eastern Zaire.
